source.title: vm expression engine: per-item parameter resolution blocks the worker event loop for minutes (lost queue locks, liveness kills)

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

With `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm`, nodes that resolve expressions for every input item spend about 2.5x longer in their synchronous parameter-resolution loop than with `legacy`. The loop doesn't yield, so on large inputs a queue-mode worker's event loop is blocked for minutes. Then:

- The Bull lock isn't renewed, so after about 30 s every job on that worker fails with `job stalled more than maxStalledCount` or `Missing key for job <id> updateProgress`. That includes unrelated executions that happen to share the worker.
- After about 2 minutes, the `/healthz` liveness probe fails and Kubernetes restarts the worker. Every execution running on it is marked `crashed`.

Two workflows trigger it for us. Both run with no problems under `legacy`.

**Case 1: Postgres node (v2.5), Execute Query, 11,034 items, 33 query parameters**

The `queryReplacement` option is set to `={{ $json.a }}, {{ $json.b }}, ... ` (33 segments). In `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Postgres/v2/actions/database/executeQuery.operation.ts`, each item does two things inside a synchronous `.map()`:

1. It resolves the whole option string with `getNodeParameter('options.queryReplacement', index)`.
2. It evaluates each of the 33 resolvables again with `this.evaluateExpression(resolvable, index)`.

That's about 34 evaluations per item, roughly 375,000 per run, before any query is sent.

| Engine | Node execution time (same workflow, same data size) |
|---|---|
| legacy | 105–111 s (includes ~11k async queries) |
| vm | 265 s |

**Case 2: Postgres node (v2), Insert or Update, 73,366 items, ~20 mapped columns**

| Engine | Node execution time |
|---|---|
| legacy | 212 s |
| vm | ~600 s |

The extra time is all synchronous. It works out to roughly 0.4–0.7 ms per `vm` evaluation for a simple `{{ $json.field }}`, against a fraction of that under `legacy`. Each evaluation in `IsolatedVmBridge.execute` does several things:

- It creates three new `ivm.Callback`s and a `HostDataResolver`.
- It runs `evalClosureSync` on a freshly wrapped script.
- It makes at least two host round trips: `$json` returns `Object.keys` of the whole item, then the field itself.

The 5 s per-expression timeout doesn't help here, because no single evaluation is slow. The cost is their number, inside one loop with no awaits.

### To Reproduce

1. Run n8n 2.46.5 in queue mode with one worker and `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm`.
2. Create a workflow with:
   - **Code node:** returns 10,000 items, each with about 40 string fields.
   - **Postgres node:** v2.5 or later, operation Execute Query, query `select $1, $2, ... $33`. Under Options → Query Parameters, set `={{ $json.f1 }}, {{ $json.f2 }}, ..., {{ $json.f33 }}`.
3. Execute it. While it runs, start any other short workflow on the same worker.
4. Watch the worker logs and its event-loop lag.
5. Repeat the run with `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=legacy` and compare the Postgres node's execution time.

Observed with `vm`:
- The Postgres node takes about 2.5x longer.
- The event loop is blocked for most of that time.
- Concurrent jobs on the worker fail with `Missing key for job ... updateProgress`.
- With big enough inputs, the liveness probe restarts the worker.

### Expected behavior

`vm` per-item expression resolution should cost about as much as `legacy`, or at least not block the event loop long enough to lose queue locks.

Possible directions:
- Reuse callbacks or the context across evaluations within one node execution.
- Batch per-item evaluation inside the isolate.
- Yield between items in nodes that resolve parameters per item.
- In the Postgres v2.5+ Execute Query path, avoid resolving the `queryReplacement` string twice.

### Debug Info

- `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm`. Pool size, timeout and memory limit are at their defaults.
- Queue settings (`QUEUE_WORKER_LOCK_DURATION` and related) are at their defaults.
- Liveness probe: `/healthz`, period 20 s, failure threshold 6, timeout 5 s.
- Changing only `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE` back to `legacy` makes the stalls and restarts stop.
- Related but different: #41322 (isolate acquisition latency on webhooks). #42571, the per-evaluation path resolution fix, is included in 2.46.5 and doesn't fix this.

### Operating System
Linux (Kubernetes, official `n8nio/n8n` image)

### n8n Version
2.46.5

### Node.js Version
26.12.1

### Database
PostgreSQL

### Execution mode
queue

### Hosting
self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current Postgres v2 `execute()` path. For each item it first calls `getNodeParameter("options.queryReplacement", index)`, then, for node version 2.5+, reads the raw configured value and evaluates each resolvable again. That matches the duplicate resolution path described here; the initially resolved value is otherwise used mainly for the type/error branches. It may be worth checking whether the 2.5+ path can branch on the raw configured value before resolving it, while keeping the older-version behavior unchanged.

comments.author: xh123637
comments.text:
Hi, I traced the duplicate resolution path you pointed out in the Postgres v2.5+ Execute Query path: for each item, `getNodeParameter('options.queryReplacement', index)` resolves the whole option string, and then the 2.5+ branch reads the raw configured value and evaluates each resolvable again with `evaluateExpression`. The initially resolved value is otherwise only used for the type/error branches, so the second pass is doing the same work twice.

I'd like to fix it along the direction you suggested — branch on the raw configured value before resolving it for node version 2.5+, while keeping the older-version behavior unchanged. Would that direction be welcome? If so, I'll open a PR with a regression test.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: Yes, that looks like a reasonable, focused direction for the v2.5+ path. Please open a PR with a regression test for the per-item expression case, and check that the older-version behavior stays unchanged.
